items.title: LIC’s ₹15.5 lakh crore portfolio revealed: Stocks India’s largest domestic investor bought and sold in Q2
items.description: Life Insurance Corporation of India made significant changes to its equity portfolio during the September quarter. The insurer invested in companies such as Larsen & Toubro, Reliance Industries, and Bharti Airtel, while selling shares in ICICI Bank, State Bank of India, and Nestle India. Despite a decline in overall portfolio value, LIC continues to be India’s largest domestic investor.

items.title: Tata Power shares rise 2% after Q2 results. Why brokerages are bullish despite target price cuts
items.description: Tata Power achieved a 33% year-on-year increase in net profit for the second quarter of FY27. Revenue also rose by 26% year-on-year to ₹19,886 crore during this period. Brokerages maintained their 'Buy' ratings while adjusting their target prices based on the latest performance figures. The company's EBITDA saw a modest growth of 5% year-on-year to ₹4,245 crore. Overall, Tata Power's market capitalisation exceeds ₹1.

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 5 stocks close above their 200 DMA
items.description: On November 11, five stocks in the Nifty 500 pack gained over 5% and crossed above their respective 200-day moving averages (DMA), according to StockEdge’s technical scan data.The 200-day moving average is a widely tracked technical indicator used to assess a stock’s long-term trend. A move above this level is generally considered a positive signal, suggesting a potential improvement in the stock’s price momentum.

items.title: MSCI rejig: LIC, Meesho, Coforge set to gain from index inclusion. How much inflows could they attract?
items.description: MSCI’s November index rejig will add LIC, Coforge, Meesho and Adani Green to its Standard Index, while removing PI Industries. Nuvama estimates the changes could trigger around $2 billion in passive inflows into Indian equities. Several stocks will also see weight adjustments, while the Smallcap Index will witness fresh additions and exclusions, creating potential stock-specific inflows and outflows.

items.title: Bajaj Finance unveils share sale to raise up to $1.25 billion
items.description: Bajaj Finance has launched a share sale to raise up to ₹117 billion from institutional investors. This offering marks a significant event following a major IPO by Jio Platforms last month. The proceeds will be allocated toward repaying various financial obligations, including loans and debentures. A team of financial institutions is collaborating with Bajaj Finance on this transaction. Additionally, the Indian equity market remains active, having raised approximately $50.

items.title: These mid-caps have ‘strong buy’ & ‘buy’ recos and an upside potential of over 25%, according to analyst
items.description: No doubt, the mood in the market has changed and the bulls seem to be back in a determined fashion. Don’t, however, expect the indices to keep climbing daily. There will be pauses. Also, though the things troubling the market have receded for now, they can still return. And these troubles are likely to be global rather than local.

items.title: Sensex, Nifty hit 8-month highs as banks, auto stocks rally
items.description: Indian equities have seen significant gains recently, with the Sensex and Nifty reaching their highest levels since February. Heavyweight stocks in the banking and auto sectors contributed to this rally amid declining crude oil prices. Profit booking was expected as investors took some money off the table after the sharp market movements. Foreign investors purchased nearly $7 billion worth of Indian equities during this period.

items.title: Stocks in news: Tata Power, Cupid, Garden Reach, ITC, Aurobindo Pharma and Vodafone Idea
items.description: Indian benchmark indices have extended their winning streak, closing positively after the Muhurat trading session. Key stocks such as life insurance companies and Tata Power reported notable quarterly earnings results. HDFC Life and LIC showed healthy premium growth, while Tata Power recorded a record profit in Q2 FY27. Other companies like Cupid and Mishra Dhatu Nigam also reported impressive profit increases during the quarter.

items.title: D-St set for a cautious opening as GIFT Nifty signals muted start
items.description: On Wednesday, Nifty closed up by 0.8%, influenced by profit booking in IT and realty stocks. Analysts indicate that Indian equities will continue to gain from improving earnings and foreign investments. The support levels for Nifty are set between 25100-25050, while hurdles are identified at 25250-25300. Additionally, foreign portfolio investors significantly increased their buying, while domestic investors sold shares.

items.title: Indications of ‘parallel power centres’: Recent succession calls spotlight Noel's rift with Tata Sons
items.description: Tata Sons has been caught off guard by the appointment of new chairpersons at three Noel Tata-led group companies without the holding company's customary approval. The appointments, made as Noel Tata stepped down as chairman at 70, have sharpened tensions between him and Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran over control and succession decisions.

items.title: PSBs improve profitability but fail to bridge valuation gap with private peers
items.description: The market continues to reward private lenders for their ability to generate higher returns through better customer service, stronger pricing power and a more consistent track record of value creation.

items.title: NCLT rejects Reliance Infra subsidiary's resolution plan
items.description: The Mumbai bench of the NCLT rejected the resolution plan for SU Toll Road Pvt Ltd due to financial concerns. These concerns were primarily related to overdue road repairs that the successful resolution applicant refused to cover. The tribunal directed lenders to decide on the next steps within 15 days following the order. Furthermore, it specified that inviting fresh bids would extend the resolution process by an additional 120 days.

items.title: Tata Electronics in talks to raise $2 billion for expansion
items.description: The first tranche is likely to be up to $800 million, with initial pricing discussions around SOFR plus 180 basis points. The talks are at an early stage, with the final size, pricing and lender participation yet to be firmed up. The loan could be priced at around 6%, assuming SOFR remains at around 3.9%.
